label: D1 after a1->S2 unrewarded, ramping linearly with episode trial past ~85
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, None) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == -1) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, None) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, None)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.4% of steps), active only at D1 in the last ~15 trials of the episode. Its magnitude is almost entirely the interaction of a previous trial a1 -> S2 (rare) unrewarded with a linear ramp in episode trial starting at ~85 (about +0.12 per trial, reaching ~1.5-2.0 by trial 96-99); this single term gives dev R^2 beyond timing 0.71. Small additions: unrewarded first-window-trial D1s (previous choice outside the window, probably the same pattern) at a weaker ramp, and a slight extra boost when the trial before that was also unrewarded. Other previous-trial patterns (any rewarded trial, a1 S1 u, a2 anything) stay at ~0. GO and D2 are always 0. Value, policy logit, an a1 S1 u term and a step onset did not add (<0.01). Additive per-cue tables top out at 0.09 (all) because they miss the pattern x late-episode interaction. All terms observed-only. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.735.

issues: Small inaccuracy: the explanation says the policy logit added less than 0.01. That is true only as an additive term. As an interaction, last_is('a1 S2 u')*ramp*choice raises test R^2 from 0.735 to 0.752 with the other two terms, and from 0.721 to 0.738 on its own. So a larger a1 logit modestly scales the ramp.

The single core term scores 0.721 on test (the label claims 0.71 on dev), which matches. Variants support the shape: the threshold works best near 85 (80: 0.682, 88: 0.700), a step (ep_trial>=86) gives only 0.540, and a capped or binned ramp does not beat the linear one. The binned weights 0.34, 0.79, 1.22 and 1.60 for trials 86-90, 91-93, 94-96 and 97-99 confirm a roughly linear rise.

Specificity holds. Swapping the pattern for 'prev unrewarded & prev_state==S2' gives 0.25, and 'prev unrewarded & prev_action==a1' gives 0.35. Value, good state and the action/state two trials back each add less than 0.005.

The worst misses are almost all D1s on the window's first trial, where the previous trial is outside the window. This is the unobserved case the second term covers, so it is not a new error class. The mean errors are about -0.01 at D1 for the other previous-trial patterns. These come from the timing baseline spreading the late-D1 mean across them, not from the explanation, and confirm they stay near 0.

About 25% of the variance beyond timing is still unexplained (for example, an a1 S2 u D1 at trial 95 predicted 1.25 but actually 0). Misses show no systematic phase, previous-trial or policy class behind this.
